Triage (route-A pass): appended `domain:metadata` — **routing only; the `finding` grade is unchanged and no ownership is taken.**

**Landing anchor (read, not guessed).** The merge key under discussion is live on `origin/main` @ `098b629`: `metaItemKey(packageId, name)` at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:988` (NUL-separated `(package, name)`, no locale discriminator), consumed by both `itemMap.set(metaItemKey(...))` loops in the unscoped list merge. The fix — a per-type discriminator-aware key, with the table homed in a shared package — lands in `packages/metadata-protocol` (+ possibly `packages/metadata-core`, already a dependency of metadata-protocol, confirmed in its `package.json`), both `domain:metadata`.

**One premise note for the grading/dispatch reader.** `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` does **not** exist on `origin/main` yet (grep zero-hit, counter-probed against `discriminator`/`locale` in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) — it rides in #7730's in-flight branch (`claude/issue-7730-registry-locale-key`, confirmed via `ls-remote`). The card is internally consistent about this ("found while fixing #7730"; the collapse only becomes reachable once the registry keeps the bundle), but any dispatch of this card is effectively sequenced behind #7730's merge, and the table's home decision (`metadata-core` re-export vs move) should be made against the merged shape.

**Dedup.** #7730 (dispatched — registry side, distinct layer), #7731/#7733 (email-template render/materialize defects, different paths). No open card covers the list-merge collapse. Not a duplicate.

Findings triage: **promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`** (`domain:metadata` stays).

**Premise re-check at `origin/main` @ `31fb03d` (the merge that changed this card's reachability):** the masking condition this card was filed behind is now gone — #7730's fix (PR #7775) merged at `31fb03d`, so `SchemaRegistry` now keeps i18n bundle members under `(name, locale)` keys and `listItems('email_template')` returns all locales. Meanwhile `metaItemKey` at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:988` is confirmed unchanged (NUL-separated `(package, name)`, no locale discriminator; consumers at `:4363` / `:4377` unchanged). The collapse this card describes is therefore **reachable today** on `GET /meta/email_template` whenever a `metadata` service returns a non-empty list — no longer a dormant observation.

**Why queue and not a decision card:** the fix location is named, and the one open question (where the `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` table lives so `metadata-protocol` can share it) has an obvious in-card answer — `@objectstack/metadata-core`, already a dependency of both — which is an implementation-placement choice, not a public-contract call. If the dev finds `metadata-core` wrong at implementation time, that's a one-line escalation then.

**Dedup:** no other open card covers the protocol-layer merge key (checked open issues for email_template/i18n bundle overlap; #7730 closed by the merged PR).

- Session: `session_01AmES43BMDg4bPrxTdi5q7t`
- Branch: `claude/issue-7774-metaitemkey-locale`

- Container & model: **M** ⇒ `mode:cloud`, `model: opus`
- Serial constraints cleared: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is **free** — #7814, #7819 and #7134 have all landed and no open PR holds it. ⚠️ **#7491 also holds this file** (`:2632`, a comment line) and is therefore **queued behind this card**, not dispatched alongside it. Disjoint from #7728 (`packages/spec`) and #7544/#7909 (`platform-objects/apps/**`).

## ⭐ Every precondition re-measured at source — the promotion note was right, and here is the proof

Promotion ≠ verified, so I re-ran the 19:07Z promoter's claims on `origin/main` rather than inheriting them:

| Claim | Probe | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| #7730 / PR #7775 merged | `git log --grep='(#7775)' --format='%h %p %s'` | `31fb03d`, **single parent** `518ca7a` ✅ |
| `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` now exists | `git grep` | `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:929`, exported, `Record<string, {field, canonical}>`, one entry: `email_template: { field: 'locale', canonical: 'en-US' }` ✅ |
| `metaItemKey` still has no discriminator | read `protocol.ts:988` | `` `${packageId ?? ''}�${String(name)}` `` — unchanged ✅ |
| `metadata-core` is a dependency of `metadata-protocol` | `package.json` | ✅ |

⇒ **The collapse is reachable today.** This is not a dormant observation.

## ⚖️ Ruling — the table's home is `@objectstack/metadata-core`, and this is not re-litigable

The card and the promoter both proposed it; I measured that it is actually *buildable*, which neither did:

- `@objectstack/objectql` **depends on** `@objectstack/metadata-core` ✅
- `@objectstack/metadata-core` depends on **only** `@objectstack/spec` + `zod` — it is a near-leaf ✅
- ⇒ **no cycle.** The table can genuinely move down into `metadata-core`, with `objectql` re-exporting it so its public surface is unchanged.

⛔ **Do not add `@objectstack/objectql` as a dependency of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`** to reach the table. That is the shortcut this card was split off #7730 specifically to avoid.

Whether you **move** the table or **move + re-export from `objectql`** is yours to choose — but `objectql`'s existing public export must keep working (see the gate below for why that is not optional).

## 🔬 PM mechanism assumption — measure it, and falsify it if it is wrong

> The fix is: give `metaItemKey` the discriminator when the type declares one — `(package, name, locale)` for `email_template`, unchanged for every other type — leaving the `sys_metadata` overlay merge at `:4207` alone, because overlay rows are unique on `type+name+org` and carry no locale.

That last clause is the card author's claim and **I have not verified it**. If the overlay merge *can* see two locales of one template, this fix is incomplete and the honest product is a wider change plus a note saying so. Measure before editing.

⚠️ Two further things I did **not** verify and you should not assume:
1. `metaItemKey` is called at `:4363` and `:4377` per the card — **re-read those call sites**; `protocol.ts` took 6 merges in a day and line anchors go stale within hours. **Anchor on function names, never line numbers.**
2. The discriminator lives next to a `@`-separator convention and a `bundleBaseKey` parser in `registry.ts`. If keying at the protocol layer needs that parsing too, moving *only* the table may leave a half-import. Decide deliberately and say which you did.

## ⛔ Gate list — read this, it is where I got a card red last round

Name gates by **what exercises the symbol**, not what mentions the path. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` cannot find a consumer suite in another package, and that exact blind spot turned #7857's first head red. Measured for you:

| Gate | Why it is on the list |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` | the change |
| `@objectstack/metadata-core` | the table's new home |
| ⭐ **`@objectstack/objectql`** | `registry-i18n-bundle-key.test.ts` imports `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` **by name** and pins `Object.keys(ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS)).toEqual(['email_template'])`. A move that does not preserve that export **breaks a suite in a package you never edited.** |
| `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/cli` | consumers of the `/meta` list face |

## ⚠️ There is no existing test for this path — you are writing the first

`git grep metaItemKey` across all of `packages/` returns **one file**: `protocol.ts` itself. No suite exercises the unscoped list merge by that key. Two consequences:

- A green run proves nothing about this defect until **you** add the failing case. Reverse-verify: commit the fix, then re-introduce the undiscriminated key and show the new test goes red naming the collapse.
- The reproduction needs a `metadata` service installed and returning a non-empty list for the type — the merge block is **skipped otherwise**, so a test that omits it will pass against the bug.

## Suggested route (optional — reject it if measurement says otherwise)

Give the key function the type, look the discriminator up, and append the canonical-normalized discriminator value only when the type declares one. Every non-discriminated type keeps a byte-identical key, which makes the blast radius provable rather than argued.

## Repricing question

Does your change make **#7491** (the two stale `AUTHORING_RULES` comment counts, one of them at `protocol.ts:2632`) simpler, harder, unnecessary, or unaffected? ⛔ Do **not** fix it here — it is a separate card and bundling it widens this PR's declared surface. I only need to know whether landing this moves its anchor.

## 1. The ruling held, and it built

`ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` now lives in `packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts`; `registry.ts` re-exports it under its original name from its original module. **`@objectstack/objectql` was never added as a dependency of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.**

One choice the ruling left to me, and which way I went: **the table moved, the storage-key FORMAT did not.** `BUNDLE_KEY_SEPARATOR`, `withDiscriminator`, `bundleBaseKey` and `collectBundle` stay in `registry.ts`. The reason is that the protocol layer never parses a registry key — it builds its own NUL-separated merge key — so what it needs is the *identity* question answered (`itemDiscriminator(type, item)`), not the encoding. Moving the encoding would have published a registry-internal Map-key format as a cross-package contract for no consumer. This is the "half-import" you flagged; it is deliberate, and the TSDoc on both sides says which half went and why, so the next reader is not left guessing.

What did move with the table: `discriminatorValue` → `readDiscriminatorValue`, plus a new `itemDiscriminator(type, item)` that applies the canonical normalization both sides were open-coding. `registry.ts` now imports the shared reader instead of keeping its own copy, so there is one definition of "what value does this item declare", not two.

## 2. The mechanism assumption — measured, and it is wrong

> *"The `sys_metadata` overlay merge at `:4207` needs no change: overlay rows are unique on `type+name+org` and carry no locale."*

**The claim about the rows is TRUE. The conclusion about the merge is FALSE.** Probes:

| Probe | Command / read | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Overlay row uniqueness | read `idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active` in `packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata.object.ts` | `(type, name, organization_id, package_id)`. **No locale column exists anywhere in `sys_metadata`** — the card's premise, confirmed at source |
| What the row-level `metaItemKey` calls actually dedupe | read the env-wide ⊕ org loops | only whether an org row shadows an env-wide row of the same name. Within one org the DB already forbids a second row ⇒ that half really is nearly inert |
| What `mergePackageAwareOverlay` buckets | read the function | `push(item.name, …)` over **`baseItems`** — and `baseItems` is `registry.listItems(type)`, which since #7730 is the **whole bundle** |
| What it then emits | read the output loop | one row per `(bucket, package)` |

So the collapse in the overlay path has nothing to do with the overlay rows. **A single, unrelated, perfectly-unique overlay row for the type is enough to drop a locale**, because the merge flattens the *base* bundle into one bucket — and the row that survives is the overlay body regardless of which member it customizes. The card reasoned about the higher layer; the defect is in the lower one.

The honest product is therefore wider than the card's route: **four keying sites**, not two.

| Site (all inside `getMetaItems`) | Change |
|:--|:--|
| MetadataService merge — the `itemMap` loops | third key component (the path the card names) |
| `mergePackageAwareOverlay` — active overlays | bucket is now a slot, `name` + discriminator |
| `mergePackageAwareOverlay` — draft preview | same slot |
| env-wide ⊕ org row dedup | `storedRowDiscriminator(type, row)`, read off the row's serialized body |

The fourth is the only one that is a genuine *semantic* widening. Within one org it cannot fire (the unique index). Across the env-wide and org tiers it can: two rows customizing **different** members of one bundle were keyed together, so an org's zh-CN row silently displaced an env-wide en-US one. Org-over-env precedence is untouched where it was ever meaningful — a case pins that an org row still overrides the env-wide row of the *same* member. Checked before relying on it: **no ADR-0087 conversion entry touches `email_template`**, so reading `locale` off the raw stored body equals reading it off the converted body.

Every non-discriminated type keeps a **byte-identical** key: `metaItemKey`'s third argument is optional and omitted, and the slot degenerates to the bare name. Four test cases assert exactly that, and all four stay green under the revert — which is the evidence, not the claim.

## 3. Call sites re-read by name, as instructed

Your warning was right in spirit and, this time, not in fact — and then became right again. At dispatch the card's `:4363`/`:4377` still pointed at the two `itemMap` loops. Mid-task `origin/main` moved 11 commits and `protocol.ts` shifted; every anchor in this report and in the PR is a **function name** (`getMetaItems`, `metaItemKey`, `mergePackageAwareOverlay`, `storedRowDiscriminator`), never a line.

## 4. Reverse verification — committed first, then broken

Fix committed as `dd64b71`. Then the undiscriminated key was re-introduced **on top of the commit** (never against an uncommitted edit), three ways, tests untouched.

| Case | revert both | `metaItemKey` only | overlay slot only |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| precondition: one discriminated type today | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| precondition: neither merge block runs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| service merge: keeps both locales | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| service merge: service contributes a new locale | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| overlay: keeps every member with ONE overlay row | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| overlay: sibling in another package survives | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| overlay: env-wide + org rows of different locales | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| overlay: org still overrides env for the SAME locale | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| overlay: no-locale member is the canonical member | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| draft preview: sibling survives | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| ADR-0048: two packages ship `page/home` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| ADR-0048: overlay collapses onto its own package slot | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| undiscriminated: same-name page is ONE row | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| | **5 red / 8** | **3 red / 10** | **3 red / 10** |

Naming the collapse:

```
FAIL  the MetadataService merge (the path the card names) > keeps both locales
AssertionError: expected [ 'auth.welcome@zh-CN', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ 'auth.welcome@en-US', …(2) ]
-   "auth.welcome@en-US",
    "auth.welcome@zh-CN",
    "billing.invoice@en-US",
```

The middle two columns are the attribution that matters to your ruling: the `metaItemKey`-only revert leaves the **overlay** cases green, and the slot-only revert leaves the **service** cases green. They are two independent collapses, which is why fixing only the card's named path would have shipped half a fix with a green suite.

Three cases stay green under the full revert and I am not dressing that up: `sibling in another package` is separated by ADR-0048's *package* dimension, which the revert does not touch, and the other two assert that the fix did **not** split things it shouldn't.

You were also right that the reproduction is conditional. The MetadataService block needs a `metadata` service installed **and** answering non-empty for the type; the overlay block needs at least one matching `sys_metadata` row. The suite carries a case (`serves the bundle when NEITHER merge block runs`) that passes on `origin/main` too, kept deliberately as the shape of harness that made this invisible.

## 5. Gates — run twice, second time in full

First on `dd64b71`+`21fc024`. Then `origin/main` moved 11 commits, two of which land inside packages I reason about (`protocol.ts` via #7906's `$icontains`; a 345-line rewrite of `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` via #7921), so per your instruction the **full** set was re-run on merge commit `3319a62`, not a scoped subset. Post-merge numbers:

| Gate | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/metadata-core` | 9 files / 129 ✅ |
| `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` | 74 files / 1082 ✅ |
| ⭐ `@objectstack/objectql` | 187 files / 3319 ✅ — `registry-i18n-bundle-key.test.ts` green, `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` by-name import and the `toEqual(['email_template'])` pin both intact |
| `@objectstack/runtime` | 139 files / 2127 ✅ |
| `@objectstack/cli` | 111 files / 1191 ✅ |
| `typecheck` × metadata-core, objectql, runtime, cli | ✅ clean |
| `check:type-check-coverage` | ✅ |
| `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` | ✅ 36 entries, 1987 raw errors, none above recorded |
| `eslint` on changed files | ✅ |
| `check:i18n` | ✅ 9 packages |
| `check:nul-bytes` | ✅ 7251 files |
| `spec check:generated` | ✅ 13/13 |
| `pnpm build` | ✅ 71/71 |

**One gate went red and I want it on the record rather than buried.** The pre-merge `check:type-check-debt` failed: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` measured **73** against a frozen **63**. All ten were mine — the new test's `row()` helper took `Partial<Row> & { metadata: unknown }`, and the intersection collapsed `metadata` to `string`, so every object body was a TS2322. Repaired with `Omit<Partial<Row>, 'metadata'>` in `21fc024`; the ledger was **not** raised. `metadata-protocol` has no `typecheck` script (it is a DEBT entry), so this ratchet is the only thing that would have caught it — worth knowing for the next card that adds a test file there.

## 6. Beyond the declared file surface

Declared surface was `metadata-protocol` + `metadata-core` + tests + changeset. Actually touched, all six files:

- `packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts` **(new)**, `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.i18n-bundle-list-merge.test.ts` **(new, 13 cases)**
- `.changeset/meta-list-i18n-bundle-key.md`
- ⚠️ **`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`** — beyond the declared surface, and unavoidable: the table's old home has to stop declaring it and start re-exporting it, or your ⭐ gate breaks. −27/+19 lines, no behaviour change; the only functional edit is that it now imports the shared value reader instead of keeping its own copy.

No `content/docs/releases/` edit. No `git stash`. No ADR touched. All work in the dedicated worktree.

**Filed, not fixed: #7932.** `duplicatePackage`'s source-row scan dedupes env-wide ⊕ org rows with the same locale-blind `(type, name)` key — same defect class, different feature and endpoint. Bundling it would have widened this PR's surface, so it is an unassigned finding with the measurement attached.

## 7. Repricing — #7491 is **unaffected in substance, and its anchor moves**

Short answer: **unaffected** — neither simpler nor harder, and definitely not unnecessary. But the line number in the card is already dead and this PR pushes it further.

| | Line of the `26 shared AUTHORING_RULES` comment |
|:--|:--|
| as recorded on #7491 | `protocol.ts:2632` |
| `origin/main` @ `d447939`, before I touched anything | **`:2698`** (+66 — drifted on its own) |
| this branch | **`:2769`** (+71 more) |

So #7491's anchor was stale *before* dispatch and this PR moves it again. The defect itself is untouched and still real: I counted `AUTHORING_RULES` at **38** entries (`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`, read via the built export) against the comment's "26". Nothing in my diff makes that comment easier or harder to fix — it is a different region of the file with no shared symbol. Whoever takes #7491 should re-find it by grepping `AUTHORING_RULES`, not by line, and should expect to rebase past this PR.
